### Q2 — CORE number variant — LCNRV schedule and initial period-end JE
**LO:** LO 10-1  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin — LCNRV by item/category/total and period-end allowance JE  
**Scenario:**  
**Lakeshore Pet Supply LLC** uses **average cost** for inventory (not LIFO/retail). December 31 data:

| Item | Category | Cost | NRV |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Grain Blend | Dry Food | $36,000 | $32,500 |
| Senior Blend | Dry Food | 21,000 | 23,000 |
| Chew Rope | Accessories | 14,500 | 15,800 |
| Puzzle Toy | Accessories | 29,000 | 26,500 |
| **Total** | | **$100,500** | **$97,800** |

COGS before LCNRV adjustment: **$255,000**. Policy: individual-item LCNRV; allowance account; charge **COGS**.

**Required:**  
(a) Compute LCNRV by item, by category, and in total; state the write-down under the item approach.  
(b) Record the Dec 31 period-end adjusting entry (item approach).  
(c) Present Inventory, net on the balance sheet and COGS after adjustment.

### Q2 — CORE number variant — Lakebound Merchants: perpetual MA, FIFO, LIFO
**LO:** LO 9-5  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin — perpetual moving average, FIFO, and LIFO schedules; purchase recognition and LIFO COGS settlement JEs  
**Scenario:**  
**Lakebound Merchants Inc.** maintains perpetual inventory records for a camping stove SKU. Purchases are on account (gross method). October activity:

| Date | Transaction | Units | Unit cost / SP |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Oct 1 | Beginning inventory | 500 | $8 cost |
| Oct 6 | Purchase on account | 300 | $10 cost |
| Oct 12 | Credit sale | 400 | $18 selling price |
| Oct 18 | Purchase on account | 500 | $11 cost |
| Oct 25 | Credit sale | 450 | $19 selling price |
| Oct 30 | Purchase on account | 100 | $12 cost |

**Required:**  
(a) Compute October **ending inventory** and **COGS** under (1) **moving average**, (2) **FIFO**, and (3) **LIFO** perpetual. Show the inventory balance (and unit cost or layers) after each purchase and after each sale.  
(b) Prepare **initial recognition** journal entries for the three purchases.  
(c) Prepare **sales and COGS** journal entries for Oct 12 and Oct 25 **under LIFO**.  
(d) Confirm COGAS − EI = COGS for all three methods.

### Q1 — CORE — Period-end AJs for litigation (best estimate + recognized subsequent event) and multi-year assurance warranty
**LO:** LO 15-5  
**Concept:** Period-end adjusting JEs for probable/estimable litigation; recognized subsequent-event remeasurement dated year-end; settlement JE; assurance-type warranty period-end accruals and subsequent measurement liability schedule  
**Scenario:**  
**Ironwood Consumer Products** is a calendar-year company. Year 1 financial statements are **issued March 10, Year 2**. Ignore income taxes and COGS.

**Litigation**  
In **October Year 1**, a delivery-vehicle accident injured a third party. A lawsuit seeking **$350,000** was filed in **December Year 1**. Counsel concludes a loss is **probable**. At December 31, Year 1, the reasonably estimable range is **$90,000 to $280,000**, and counsel’s **better estimate** within the range is **$120,000**.

On **February 18, Year 2** (before FS issuance), the parties agree to settle for **$145,000** cash, payable **May 1, Year 2**.

**Assurance-type warranty**  
Ironwood’s products include a **two-year assurance-type warranty** against manufacturing defects (not sold separately). Estimated warranty cost = **2.0% of product sales**. Actual claims are paid in cash. Accruals are recorded as **period-end adjusting entries** each December 31.

| Year | Product sales (cash) | Actual warranty claims paid |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | $3,200,000 | $18,000 |
| 2 | 3,600,000 | 52,000 |
| 3 | 4,000,000 | 61,000 |

Warranty rate remains 2.0% of that year’s sales each year.

**Required:**  
a. **(Emphasis)** Record the **December 31, Year 1 period-end adjusting entry** to accrue the litigation contingency using the **better estimate** (ignore the February settlement for this part only).  
b. **(Emphasis)** Record the **recognized subsequent event** remeasurement as a **December 31, Year 1 adjusting entry** after the February 18 settlement agreement.  
c. Record the **May 1, Year 2 settlement** payment.  
d. Record Year 1 **product sales**, the **December 31, Year 1 period-end warranty accrual**, and **Year 1 claims** settlement.  
e. Prepare the complete **warranty liability subsequent measurement schedule** for Years 1–3 (beginning, accrual, claims, ending).  
f. **(Emphasis)** Record the **December 31, Year 2 period-end adjusting entry** for the Year 2 warranty accrual.  
g. In one sentence: if at December 31 Year 1 the litigation loss were only **reasonably possible** (estimate still $120,000), what period-end reporting would apply?

### Q1 — CORE — Between-interest TS purchase, period-end FVA (emphasis), sale vs AC, year-end FVA cleanup

**LO:** LO 14-7  
**Concept:** Initial recognition of trading debt securities; cash interest; **period-end-only** FV-NI adjusting JE (emphasis); disposal with realized G/L vs amortized cost; subsequent period-end FVA elimination  
**Scenario:**  
**Larkspur Trading Partners** (calendar year) buys debt for short-term price appreciation and classifies it as **trading securities (TS)** measured at **FV-NI**. Per company policy (Appendix 14A / LO 14-7), Larkspur records **Fair Value Adjustment (FVA)** entries **only at each December 31 period-end**—never on sale dates.

**Facts:**
1. On **November 1, Year 1**, Larkspur purchases **at par** **$60,000** face of **Cascade Biologics** **9%** bonds (bonds dated **July 1, Year 1**; mature **June 30, Year 7**). Cash interest is paid **semiannually on June 30 and December 31**. No brokerage fees.
2. Fair value of the Cascade bonds on **December 31, Year 1** is **$57,000**.
3. On **March 15, Year 2**, Larkspur sells the entire holding for **$57,600** cash (clean price; ignore any March accrued-interest complexity beyond the facts given).
4. After the sale, Larkspur holds **no other TS**. It next adjusts FVA only on **December 31, Year 2**.

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the **November 1, Year 1 initial recognition JE** (include accrued interest paid to seller).  
b. Prepare the **December 31, Year 1** cash interest receipt JE.  
c. Prepare a **period-end FVA worksheet** and the **December 31, Year 1 period-end adjusting JE** (emphasis).  
d. Show **Year 1 balance-sheet carrying amount** and **income-statement** effects (interest + unrealized G/L).  
e. Prepare the **March 15, Year 2 disposal JE** under LO 14-7 (realized G/L vs amortized cost; **do not** adjust FVA at sale).  
f. Prepare the **December 31, Year 2 period-end adjusting JE** that eliminates leftover FVA, and a **holding-period G/L reconciliation** schedule.

### Q1 — CORE — Multi-security ranking schedule, sequential diluted EPS, initial recognition & period-end JEs (emphasis: subsequent measurement schedule)
**LO:** LO 20-9  
**Concept:** Initial recognition of convertible securities; subsequent measurement ranking and sequential diluted EPS schedules; period-end preferred dividend and bond interest JEs; dual face presentation of basic and diluted EPS  
**Scenario:**  
**Meridian Cascade Holdings Inc.** is a calendar-year public company with a **complex capital structure**. For the year ended December 31, Year 1:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Net income | $380,000 |
| Weighted-average common shares outstanding (entire year) | 200,000 |
| Income tax rate | 25% |

There are **no** discontinued operations. On **January 1, Year 1**, Meridian issued the following securities (all outstanding the entire year; none exercised or converted during Year 1). Common stock has a **$1 par** value.

1. **Employee stock options:** 10,000 options to purchase one common share each at an exercise price of **$20**. Average market price of common stock during Year 1: **$40**.
2. **5% cumulative convertible preferred stock:** 4,000 shares, **$100 par**, issued at par. Each preferred share is convertible into **3** common shares. Preferred dividends for the full year were declared and paid on December 31.
3. **Series X convertible bonds:** **$500,000** face, **4%** coupon, issued at par on January 1. Each **$1,000** bond is convertible into **25** common shares. Interest was paid in cash for the full year.
4. **Series Y convertible bonds:** **$300,000** face, **10%** coupon, issued at par on January 1. Each **$1,000** bond is convertible into **8** common shares. Interest was paid in cash for the full year.

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the **January 1, Year 1 initial recognition journal entries** for (1) the convertible preferred stock issuance and (2) the Series X convertible bond issuance. Show Dr = Cr.  
b. Compute the **numerator effect**, **denominator effect**, and **earnings per incremental share** for each potentially dilutive security. **Rank** the securities from most dilutive to least dilutive.  
c. Compute **basic EPS** for Year 1.  
d. Prepare the **sequential diluted EPS subsequent measurement schedule** (most dilutive → least dilutive). Identify which securities are dilutive vs antidilutive and state **diluted EPS**.  
e. Prepare the **December 31, Year 1 period-end journal entries** for (1) the annual preferred dividend (cash paid same day) and (2) full-year cash interest on Series X bonds. Show Dr = Cr.  
f. Show the **financial statement presentation** of basic and diluted EPS on the face of the income statement.

### Q1 — CORE — Multi-use R&D assets: initial recognition, full subsequent measurement schedules, period-end R&D charges, disposal
**LO:** LO 13-7  
**Concept:** Initial recognition of R&D (expense vs capitalize multi-use assets); full straight-line **subsequent measurement schedules** for multi-use equipment and multi-project intangible (amortization classified as R&D); period-end adjusting JEs; disposal of multi-use equipment; Year-1 R&D disclosure total  
**Scenario:**  
**Northline Photonix Corp.** (calendar year-end) conducts research and development of optical sensors. During **Year 1**, Northline incurred the following (paid in cash unless noted):

| # | Fact | Amount / term |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Materials purchased and **consumed** solely on current R&D projects (**no** alternative future use) | **$185,000** |
| 2 | Laboratory equipment purchased **January 1, Year 1** with **significant alternative future uses** (multiple future R&D projects and limited production support); residual value **$30,000**; **straight-line** over **5 years**; placed in service Jan 1 and used in R&D | **$600,000** |
| 3 | Specialized testing chamber purchased **March 1, Year 1** for a **single** R&D project only; **no** alternative future use | **$72,000** |
| 4 | Salaries and wages of scientists and technicians engaged in R&D | **$980,000** |
| 5 | Fees paid to an outside university lab for contract R&D services | **$125,000** |
| 6 | Reasonable allocation of indirect facility costs clearly related to R&D (utilities, security of R&D wing) | **$48,000** |
| 7 | Finite-life technical database / know-how license acquired **January 1, Year 1** for use across **multiple** R&D projects (alternative future uses); residual **$0**; amortize **straight-line** over **4 years**; amortization classified as R&D | **$40,000** |
| 8 | Design and construction of **preproduction prototypes** for a new sensor under development | **$44,000** |
| 9 | Quality control and troubleshooting during **commercial production** of existing products | **$35,000** |
| 10 | Corporate headquarters G&A **not** clearly related to R&D | **$200,000** |

No impairment is recognized in Years 1–3. On **January 1, Year 4**, after three full years of depreciation have been recorded, Northline **sells** the multi-use laboratory equipment (item 2) for **$240,000** cash.

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the **Year 1 initial recognition** journal entries for items 1–10 (group by treatment: expense as R&D, capitalize asset, or non-R&D expense).  
b. Prepare the **December 31, Year 1 period-end adjusting JEs** for (1) depreciation of multi-use laboratory equipment and (2) amortization of the multi-project technical license.  
c. Prepare the complete **subsequent measurement (straight-line depreciation) schedule** for the multi-use laboratory equipment for Years 1–5 (beginning book value, depreciation classified as R&D, ending book value).  
d. Prepare the complete **subsequent measurement (amortization) schedule** for the multi-project technical license for Years 1–4 (beginning CV, amortization classified as R&D, ending CV).  
e. Compute **total research and development expense** to be **disclosed** for Year 1. List major items **excluded** from R&D.  
f. Prepare the **January 1, Year 4 disposal** journal entry for the laboratory equipment (after Years 1–3 depreciation already recorded).  
g. Briefly state why depreciation of multi-use equipment is R&D expense while the equipment **purchase** is not fully expensed in Year 1.

### Q3 — CORE alternate angle — Period-end adjusting and settlement reconstructed entries only
**LO:** LO 22-6  
**Concept:** Period-end adjusting worksheet JEs (WC, depreciation, bond premium amortization); disposal of equipment; initial recognition of bonds at a discount; early bond retirement (settlement) — classify each lower-half amount O/I/F  
**Scenario:**  
**Riverside Caliper Co.** is assembling the **cash flow worksheet** for the year ended December 31, 2025 (indirect method). For each item below, prepare the **reconstructed worksheet entry** (or entries) that would appear on the worksheet. Label lower-half lines with the **section** (Operating, Investing, or Financing). Do **not** prepare a full formal SCF.

**Items:**
1. **Period-end WC:** Accounts receivable decreased **$12,000**; allowance for doubtful accounts increased **$2,000**.  
2. **Period-end WC:** Inventory increased **$6,500**.  
3. **Period-end adjusting:** Depreciation expense **$28,000** (equipment).  
4. **Disposal:** Equipment sold — original cost **$90,000**, accumulated depreciation **$55,000**, cash proceeds **$30,000**.  
5. **Initial recognition:** Issued **$80,000** face bonds payable for cash at **95** (discount **$4,000**).  
6. **Subsequent measurement / period-end:** Amortization of bond discount for the year **$800**.  
7. **Settlement:** Retired remaining bonds early — face **$80,000**, unamortized discount at retirement **$2,400**, cash paid **$79,000**.

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the reconstructed worksheet entry for each item (1)–(7). Show Dr = Cr checks.  
b. For items (1)–(7), list each amount that hits the **lower half** and classify it as **Operating add**, **Operating deduct**, **Investing inflow/outflow**, or **Financing inflow/outflow**.  
c. Compute the **net effect on operating cash flows** (indirect) from items (1)–(4) and (6)–(7) only (exclude the pure financing initial recognition in item 5’s cash proceeds from this subtotal’s “operating” count; include only the O section pieces).

### Q2 — CORE number variant — Life extended, residual cut, disposal with loss
**LO:** LO 12-4  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin: initial PPE recognition; SL schedule; prospective change in useful life and residual; updated period-end dep; disposal with loss  
**Scenario:**  
**Coastal Glassworks Inc.** (calendar year) places a tempering furnace into service on **January 1, Year 1**.

| Fact | Amount / term |
|---|---|
| Cash purchase cost | **$240,000** |
| Original residual value | **$24,000** |
| Original useful life | **8 years**, straight-line |
| **January 1, Year 5** change in estimate | Total useful life revised to **12 years**; residual revised to **$12,000** |
| Disposal | Sold for **$95,000** cash on **December 31, Year 6** (after Year 6 depreciation) |

**Required:**  
a. Initial recognition JE on January 1, Year 1.  
b. Original annual depreciation; depreciation schedule for Years 1–4.  
c. Carrying amount at January 1, Year 5; updated annual depreciation; Year 5 period-end JE.  
d. Schedule Years 5–12 (spot-check that residual is reached at end of Year 12).  
e. Disposal JE on December 31, Year 6.  
f. One-sentence classification: is this a change in principle, error correction, or estimate?

### Q1 — CORE — Year-end straddling small dividend, equity schedule, large dividend, true split
**LO:** LO 19-6  
**Concept:** Initial recognition (small at FV vs large at par); period-end equity presentation of dividends distributable; distribution settlement; true split (no JE); subsequent equity schedule  
**Scenario:**  
**SummitRidge Packaging Corp.** (calendar-year reporter) has the following stockholders’ equity on **December 15, Year 1**, immediately before any dividend or split action:

| Account | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Common stock, $3 par; 60,000 shares issued and outstanding | $180,000 |
| Paid-in capital in excess of par—common stock | 540,000 |
| Retained earnings | 750,000 |
| **Total stockholders’ equity** | **$1,470,000** |

The market price of SummitRidge common stock on December 15 is **$22 per share**. Treat **Scenarios A, B, and C independently**, each starting from the December 15 balances above.

**Scenario A — Small stock dividend straddling year-end**  
On **December 15, Year 1**, the board declares a **12%** common stock dividend. Distribution is scheduled for **January 12, Year 2**, to shareholders of record December 28. All entitlements are whole shares (no fractional shares).

**Scenario B — Large stock dividend (stock split effected in the form of a dividend)**  
On **December 15, Year 1**, the board declares a **50%** common stock dividend (additional shares = 50% of shares previously outstanding). Distribution date is **January 12, Year 2**. Market price remains $22 (do **not** use market for measurement of large dividends).

**Scenario C — True stock split**  
On **December 15, Year 1**, SummitRidge effects a **2-for-1** stock split by reducing par value per share (not structured as a stock dividend). Authorized shares are adjusted as needed for disclosure.

**Required:**  
a. **Scenario A:** Prepare the **December 15 declaration** journal entry (initial recognition at fair value). Show Dr = Cr.  
b. **Scenario A — period-end:** Identify any **December 31, Year 1 adjusting journal entry** related to this stock dividend. State how **Common Stock Dividends Distributable** is **classified/presented** on the December 31 balance sheet.  
c. **Scenario A:** Prepare a **subsequent equity / share schedule** at (1) immediately **before** declaration, (2) **December 31, Year 1** (after declaration, before distribution), and (3) **after** distribution on January 12, Year 2. Include CS, CSDD, PIC—CS, RE, total equity, shares outstanding, and par per share.  
d. **Scenario A:** Prepare the **January 12, Year 2 distribution (settlement)** journal entry.  
e. **Scenario B:** Prepare the **December 15 declaration** and **January 12 distribution** journal entries at **par**. State ending CS, PIC, RE, shares outstanding, and total equity after distribution.  
f. **Scenario C:** Journal entry (if any)? Report shares outstanding, par per share, and total common stock dollar amount after the split.

### Q2 — CORE number variant — Same lifecycle, all numbers changed
**LO:** LO 8-9  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin — initial recognition, period-end interest, DCF impairment AJE, subsequent measurement schedule, period-end effective-interest accruals, settlement  
**Scenario:**  
**Harborline Merchants** (calendar year) sold inventory to **Dunecrest Packaging** on **January 1, Year 1** and accepted a **four-year, 6%, $80,000** note at face (market rate **6%**). Interest of **$4,800** is due each December 31; principal is due **December 31, Year 4**.

Harborline collected Year 1 interest. At **December 31, Year 1**, after collecting interest, Harborline expects **no further interest** and only **$54,000** of principal on the original due date (**December 31, Year 4**). The current similar-risk market rate is **12%** (ignore for discounting). On **December 31, Year 4**, Harborline collects **exactly $54,000**.

**Required:**  
(a) Initial recognition JE (Jan 1, Y1) and Year 1 interest receipt.  
(b) Impairment computation and **period-end impairment AJE** at Dec 31, Y1 (use **PV = $45,339**).  
(c) Subsequent measurement schedule of net CA and AFDA through Dec 31, Y4 before settlement.  
(d) Period-end effective-interest AJEs for Year 2 and Year 3.  
(e) Combined settlement JE at Dec 31, Y4 (include final interest accretion).
